problem_type: Two elements in one component each hard-code the geometry of the same edge
symptom: On the clip-node timeline the first character of a clip label is covered by the trim handle: English dark theme shows "Image" as "mage", and a selected clip's 16px handle sits on top of the label.
direct_cause: The label is a full-width span with a fixed 6px side padding written in the component; the handles are absolute siblings above it whose width (8-16 screen px, zoom aware) is derived in clipNodeGestureModel.ts. Nothing tied the two numbers together.
class_root: Anything laid across the full width of a clip competes with the edge handles for the same pixels, and the handle width had exactly one derivation while the label inset had a second, independent one. Any new full-width element (duration badge, status strip) or any change of the handle width would hide content the same way.
migration: No persisted format change. The component's fixed px-1.5 on the label is deleted in the same change and replaced by clipLabelInset, derived in the gesture model from the handle width.
affected_population: Every user who selects or hovers a clip on a clip node timeline, in either language and theme
invariants: The label's side inset is clipLabelInset, which is never smaller than the clip's handle width in any state
No pixel constant for clip edge geometry lives in the component

door_reduction.why_not: One door remains by construction: the label inset is computed in the gesture model from the same function that sizes the handles.

residual_risks: Narrow clips (about 40px for 2 seconds on the default axis) show only the first character plus an ellipsis; a hover full name or moving the label out of the handle band needs an approved design.
Other full-width children added to a clip later must also read the model; no gate enforces that yet.
internal_only_reason: Pure in-house layout geometry of the clip node; no third-party behaviour involved and CSS has no mechanism to reserve space for an absolutely positioned sibling.

recurrence.reason: The handle width has changed several times in the last two weeks and every change silently shifted what the label could show.
same_class_scan: rg 'absolute inset-y-0' in ClipNodeTimeline.tsx: only the handles and the hit pads sit on the clip edge
rg 'px-' in ClipNodeTimeline.tsx: the label was the only full-width text span with its own side padding

generality_proof: The inset is a pure function of clip width and zoom taken from the handle's own derivation (selected state, the widest), so it follows any retuning of CLIP_HANDLE_MAX_HIT_PX and the share rule; the unit matrix checks it against idle and selected handle widths over zoom 0.2-3 and clip width 10-400, and the real-app walk measures glyph rectangles against handle rectangles in zh light and en dark.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Single place where the space the edge handles occupy becomes a content inset.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Fixed px-1.5 deleted; inset now clipLabelInset (clipNodeGestureModel.test.ts matrix, clip-label-under-handle.walk.mjs).
Already derives its width from clipHandleHitWidth; it is the source the label inset follows.
Shown only while resizing, centred above the clip, not inside the handle band.

prevention.invariant: The label inset and the handle width come from one derivation in the gesture model.
prevention.failure_mode: A hard-coded inset or a wider handle that the label does not follow fails the unit matrix and the real-app geometry walk.
prevention.strategy: Delete the component's own constant, derive the inset from the handle width, lock the relation with a matrix test and a glyph-rectangle walk.

legacy_paths.rationale: The fixed px-1.5 on the label was replaced in place; no file or parallel version left behind.
